propositions: The outbound differ compares in vendor shape (raw Jira snapshot keys), while the inbound differ canonicalizes via InboundMapper before comparing, creating an asymmetric design that violates ADR 0035 §(d) by keeping vendor-shaped helpers in core.

The update path (_compute_outbound_update_mutation) must canonicalize the snapshot entry via InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local before field comparison, compute changed fields in canonical (local) names, and emit vendor payloads only at the emission boundary via a new OutboundMapper.map_fields_to_remote method.

The InboundMapper output must widen to include canonical identity aliases (assignee_identity, reporter_identity) and remote_parent_id as fixed-shape dicts/strings, with presence-guarded (absence = no key in output) semantics to support partial-dict mapping of stored baseline fields.

The assignee resolver (resolver_assignee) must be re-homed to OutboundMapper as a canonical-shape-only parameterized method, preserving the 3-tuple return contract (payload_value, authoritative, is_account_id) and the _assignee_is_account_id sentinel key for the accountId fast-path.

The stored arbitration baseline stays vendor-shaped at rest but is canonicalized at read time (via InboundMapper), enabling suppression/conflict detection to work in local field names without data migration or writer changes.

Vendor-shaped comparison helpers (_diff_fields, _extract_jira_field, _assignee_matches, _LOCAL_TO_JIRA_TYPE) become adapter-internal to adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py, eliminating all vendor key literals and adapters.jira imports from outbound_differ.py.
